Here's a comprehensive overview of the **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team**, based on historical records, season reviews, and conference data. This was a landmark season marking a major turnaround for the program under head coach Kellie Harper.

### **Key Season Highlights**
- **Record:** 22–10 overall (14–4 MVC conference)
- **Conference Finish:** **MVC Regular Season Champions** (tied with UNI; won tiebreaker via head-to-head).
- **Postseason:** Earned an **at-large bid to the NCAA Tournament** (11-seed in Greensboro Region). Lost in the First Four (Round 1) to #6 seed LSU (59–55).
- **Notable Achievement:** First MVC regular-season title since 2010 and first NCAA Tournament appearance since 2012, signaling a resurgence after back-to-back losing seasons (2012–13 and 2013–14).

---

### **Coaching Staff**
- **Head Coach:** **Kellie Harper** (2nd season at MSU).  
  — Former Tennessee All-American (3x NCAA champ under Pat Summitt) and WNBA player. Took over after legendary coach Cheryl Burnett's retirement in 2011.  
  — This season cemented her reputation for defensive intensity and player development.  
- **Assistants:** Amaka Agugua (associate head coach), Jenny Lingor, and Megan Claxton.

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
The team featured a balanced mix of transfers, underclassmen, and key holdovers. Top contributors included:

1. **Brice Calip (Sr., Guard)**  
   - **Leading scorer (15.2 PPG)**, MVC First Team.  
   - Explosive shooter; hit 87 threes (41.6% 3PT), ranked top 3 in MVC.  
   - Scored 30+ points twice (vs. Indiana State, SE Missouri State).

2. **Cokny Thames (Jr., Guard)**  
   - **Second-leading scorer (14.0 PPG)**; MVC First Team.  
   - Dynamic playmaker (4.1 APG); led team in assists and steals (1.9 SPG).  
   - Had multiple 20+ point games (e.g., 24 pts vs. Evansville).

3. **Teana Muldrew (So., Forward)**  
   - **Defensive anchor** (MVC All-Defensive Team); 8.8 PPG, 5.3 RPG, 1.8 BPG, 2.0 SPG.  
   - Only player in NCAA to average 1.8+ blocks AND 2.0+ steals per game.  
   - Critical in MVC Tournament; 16 pts/9 reb vs. Drake.

4. **Madison Guebert (Sr., Forward)**  
   - Versatile leader (9.1 PPG, 5.2 RPG); MVC All-Tournament Team.  
   - Hit clutch shots; 15 pts in NCAA Tournament game vs. LSU.

5. **Shayra Brown (So., Guard)**  
   - Primary ball-handler (4.8 APG, 1.7 SPG); 5.2 PPG.  
   - Ranked top 5 in MVC for assists.

**Other Contributors:**  
- Chelsea Welch (Sr., C; 6.2 PPG, 5.9 RPG), Kelsey Hunt (So., G; 6.0 PPG), Jada Garner (Fr., G; explosive freshman scorer).  
- Transfer **Regan Greener** (Sr., G) added depth early but left the team mid-season.

---

### **Season Narrative**
- **Non-Conference (8–5):**  
  — Started strong with wins over **Oklahoma State** (73–63) and Tennessee Tech, but fell to power-conference teams (Kansas, West Virginia, Oklahoma State *in second matchup*).  
  — Losses to UMKC and Saint Louis hinted at inconsistency.  
- **MVC Dominance (14–4):**  
  — Went 12–0 at home (JQH Arena), including thrilling wins over archrival Drake (twice: 70–66 and 77–74 OT).  
  — Only losses: Road games at Evansville (1st MVC loss under Harper) and UNI. Won title via tiebreaker after UNI swept the season series.  
  — Averaged **75.2 PPG** (5th in MVC), but defense was elite (allowed 60.0 PPG; 2nd in MVC).  
- **MVC Tournament (Semifinalists):**  
  — **Beat Illinois State** in QF (79–64), but lost to **Drake 70–62** in SF. Avoided automatic NCAA snub due to strong resume.  
- **NCAA Tournament:**  
  — Drew **LSU** (SEC, 21–10) in Round 1. MSU led late in the 3rd quarter, but LSU pulled away (59–55). Calip (17 pts) and Guebert (15 pts) led scoring.

---

### **Team Style & Statistics**
- **Offense:** Relied on **three-point shooting** (ranked #18 nationally at 257 made threes; 36.3% as a team). Took 40% of shots from deep.  
- **Defense:** Pressured opponents into **16.5 turnovers/game** (MVC #1). Blocked 3.8 shots/game (MVC #2).  
- **Key Stat:** Outrebounded opponents by +4.0 RPG; 19–2 record when holding opponent under 65 points.

---

### **Postseason Accolades & Legacy**
- **Awards:**  
  — Calip & Thames: MVC First Team.  
  — Muldrew: MVC All-Defensive Team; Calip named to MVC All-Tournament Team.  
  — Harper: Co-MVC Coach of the Year (with UNI's Tanya Warren).  
- **Legacy:**  
  — Ended a **two-year NCAA drought** and regained MVC respectability after 13–17 record in 2013–14.  
  — Proved Harper could build a contender without Cheryl Burnett's legacy players (e.g., Jackie Stiles era).  
  — Laid groundwork for future success (MSU made WNIT 3x in next 5 years).

---

### **Quirks & Fun Facts**
- Only team in nation with **two players** averaging 14+ PPG, 4+ RPG, and 3+ APG (Calip & Thames).  
- Set program record for **three-pointers made in a game** (15 vs. SE Missouri State).  
- Beat Oklahoma State without Calip (suspension) — first win over Power 5 foe since 2006.  
- #12 nationally in attendance (4,550 avg.) at JQH Arena.

This season remains a **touchstone for Missouri State women’s basketball** — embodying resilience under Harper and setting the stage for MVC contention through the late 2010s. If you need play-by-play game logs, full stats, or video highlights, I can guide you to sources like the [MSU Athletics Archive](https://mostats.com/sports/wbkb/2014-15/files/) or NCAA Tournament coverage! 🏀
